thread:
sam: Brainstorm: instead of an all-or-nothing fallback, what if the continuous batcher uses a graded degrade per-tenant based on a short-term "pressure score"? Keeps most tenants in NORMAL while surgically limiting noisy ones.

rachel: I like that. How do you compute pressure score cheaply? We can't add heavy sampling per request.

sam: Combine three cheap signals in a rolling window: inflight_tokens_per_tenant, recent_kv_miss_rate, and p95_enqueue_latency. Weighted sum, downsampled to 1s bins.

tony: Can we avoid tight coupling to the coalescer internals? Proposal: a ScoreProducer interface that emits (tenant_id, score, reason) to the admission layer. Admission only sees score->action mapping.

lee: Good separation. Actions could be: NOOP, SOFT_SHRINK_WINDOW, FORCE_TINY_WINDOW, PRIORITY_DEMOTE. That way Redirecting to microfastpath is just one action.

sam: We should ensure the score is conservative: small spikes shouldn't immediately demote. Use exponential backoff on demotion and faster decay on recovery.

rachel: Edge-case: streaming/long-running requests shouldn't be demoted mid-stream. Admission must tag streaming sessions with sticky decisions for their lifetime.

tonY: (typo) Tony: +1 to sticky decisions. Also add an operator override via CLI: rdbctl batcher set-tenant-mode <tenant> <mode> for incidents.

ops-bot: ops-bot: NOTE: any operator override should emit audit log: /audit/batcher/overrides with who/when/mode.

lee: Observability: metrics to add: batcher.graded_demotions.count, batcher.tenant_score{tenant}.gauge, batcher.demoted_tenants.gauge, batcher.demote_reasons.count. Also traces: Emit a short event when action changes for a tenant.

sam: Implementation plan sketch: 1) Add ScoreProducer (inference-friendly rust module) 2) Admission accepts optional score hint: admit(request, score_hint) -> action 3) Coalescer applies action with sticky token for streaming 4) Feature-flag rollout + canary.

rachel: Testing: create harness that can drive 10k ephemeral tenants with synthetic kv miss storms and verify demotion rate and false positives <2%. We'll also test cache-warmup scenarios.

lee: Backwards compatibility: admit() keeps current signature; new optional param is backward-compatible. Default behavior if ScoreProducer absent is unchanged.

sam: Deployment model: run ScoreProducer colocated on every runtime instance so decisions are local and fast. Also a global aggregator can emit cluster-wide circuit-breaker if > threshold tenants demoted.

rachel: Concern: per-instance decisions might cause oscillation across GPUs. We need per-tenant sticky token keyed in a distributed cache (short TTL) so different workers converge. Or simply prefer local decisions but expose a global override if cluster p90 > X ms.

lee: Distributed cache adds complexity. Maybe start with local sticky decisions and a conservative global circuit-breaker. If we see divergence in canary, iterate with a lightweight gossip sync.

sam: Security/Private deploys: ScoreProducer must be opt-in; no external telemetry leaves host. All signals used are local runtime metrics. Add a runtime flag: --enable-graded-degrade.

tony: Also document the action semantics carefully: e.g., PRIORITY_DEMOTE must not starve a tenant completely; set a minimum token allocation.

ops-bot: ops-bot: canary rollout scheduled: batcher-graded-degrade-v0.1 -> canary cluster. Logs to /observability/batcher/graded_degrade.

rachel: Next steps: Sam to PR ScoreProducer interface + test harness, Lee to add metric/trace hooks, Tony to add operator override implementation and audit logs. We'll review after canary telemetry.

sam: I'll include a spreadsheet of suggested weights and thresholds and a small simulator for tuning. If the canary shows too many false demotions we'll widen hysteresis and increase decay time.

lee: Nice work. This should let us keep batch efficiency for normal tenants while protecting tail latency during KV storms without wholesale microbatch fallback.
